**The big question of the whole experiment:** which genes change between biofilm and
planktonic? The plot that answers it — and the one you'll walk out able to make — is
the **volcano plot**: fold change on x, significance on y.

## Setup {-}

```{r setup06, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
data_dir <- c("data", "../data", "project/data", "../project/data")
data_dir <- data_dir[dir.exists(data_dir)][1]
de <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "DE_biofilm_vs_planktonic_24h.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Prepare the data. (A few genes have an adjusted p-value of exactly 0; we replace those
with the smallest non-zero value so they can be plotted.)

```{r}
de_plot <- de %>%
  mutate(
    padj = ifelse(padj == 0, min(padj[padj > 0], na.rm = TRUE), padj),
    status = case_when(
      padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange >  1 ~ "Up in biofilm",
      padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange < -1 ~ "Down in biofilm",
      TRUE                              ~ "Not significant"
    )
  )
```

The volcano:

```{r}
volcano <- ggplot(de_plot, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), colour = status)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Up in biofilm"   = "firebrick",
                                 "Down in biofilm" = "steelblue",
                                 "Not significant" = "grey70")) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (biofilm vs planktonic)",
       y = "-log10(adjusted p-value)",
       colour = NULL)

volcano
```

Far-right red points = strongly **up** in biofilm; far-left blue = strongly **down**.
High up the y-axis = most confident. That single picture answers the experiment.

<div class="remember">
  <strong>📌 Principle:</strong> a good plot encodes two things at once here — effect
  size (x) and confidence (y) — so the eye finds the important genes instantly.
</div>

## Make it explorable {-}

One line turns it interactive — hover any point to see which gene it is:

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(plotly)
# add `text = gene_id` so the tooltip shows the gene you hover over
ggplotly(volcano + aes(text = gene_id), tooltip = "text")
```
